title: Day centre review, woman says minibus driver touched her (synthetic)
setting: A social worker meets Leanne Marsh, 32, who has a learning disability, in a quiet room at Brookside Day Centre, Harbridge, for her annual review, after staff noticed she had become upset about the minibus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hello Leanne. Is it okay if we sit in here? It's a bit quieter.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Is this my review?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: It is, yes. We'll talk about what you do here, home, and anything you want to change. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll write some notes as we go. Most of what you tell me stays private. But if you tell me someone's hurting you or not being nice to you, I might have to tell other people so we can help. I'd tell you first.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So what do you like doing here?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Art. I'm doing a big painting. It's of my cat, Biscuit.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Oh, I'd love to see it after. What else?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Cooking on Mondays. And the disco on Friday.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And at home, is it still you and your mum?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Mum's knees are bad now. I help her with the hoovering.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's kind of you. Are you still doing the travel training?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Sometimes. I want to get the bus on my own. To town.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's a good goal. How do you get here at the moment?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: The minibus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How's the minibus?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Um.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Sue said you got a bit upset about the bus last week. Do you want to tell me about it?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I don't like Dave.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Who's Dave?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He drives it. The minibus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. What is it you don't like about Dave?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He does things.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Can you tell me what sort of things?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He. He touched me.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you for telling me, Leanne. Where did he touch you?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Here. On my chest. On the minibus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: On your chest. Where was the minibus when that happened?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Outside my house. When I'm getting off.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Did he touch you anywhere else?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Um. Between my legs. Over my trousers.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. You're doing really well.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. No, I'm telling stories. Forget it. I'm telling stories.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: That's alright. You don't have to say anything you don't want to. Can I ask what made you say you're telling stories?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Dave said nobody would believe me.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'm listening to you, Leanne. Was it a story?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. It's true. He did. He touched me between my legs.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. Did Dave do anything else?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He kissed me. On my mouth. I didn't like it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Did Dave say anything to you?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He said it's our secret. Our secret, and don't tell Mum.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How often has Dave done these things?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Every week. When I'm the last one on the bus.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: When you're the last one on the bus?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. The others get off first. Then it's just me. Every week.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: When did it start, can you remember?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: After the summer. After my birthday in August.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. I need to ask you something else, Leanne. Has anyone else touched you like that? Any of the staff here?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Not the staff. They're nice.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So none of the staff at Brookside have ever touched you like that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. Only Dave. Nobody else.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Thank you. You've been really brave telling me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Am I in trouble?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: No. You haven't done anything wrong. Dave shouldn't have done that.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I need to tell some people so we can keep you safe. The safeguarding team at the council, and the police. Is that alright?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: The police?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: They help keep people safe. If they want to talk to you, I'll make sure there's someone with you who helps you understand.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Can I tell your mum?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Will she be cross?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I don't think she'll be cross with you. I can talk to her with you if you like.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, you do it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. And from tomorrow you won't be going on Dave's bus. Can your mum bring you, or would you like a taxi?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: A taxi. Mum can't drive with her knees.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. So, here's what's going to happen. Today, I'll ring the safeguarding team and the police. I'll talk to Joanne, the centre manager, so she can arrange a taxi from tomorrow, Wednesday.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll come to your house tomorrow at 4 o'clock and we'll tell your mum together.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. Can Biscuit be there?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Of course. And we'll carry on with the travel training plan. I'll ask Sue to set up two practice bus trips into town in December.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I like that.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Good. And I'll bring you something easy-read about what happens next.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Can I go back to art now?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Yes. Thank you for talking to me, Leanne.

disclosures.what: Leanne said the minibus driver, Dave, touched her on her chest on the minibus outside her house.
Leanne said Dave touched her between her legs over her trousers, then said she was telling stories, then restated that it was true.
Leanne said Dave kissed her on the mouth and told her it was their secret and not to tell her mum.
Leanne said this happens every week when she is the last one on the bus, and started after her birthday in August.

controls.must_not_claim: Day centre staff have touched Leanne.
